primitives.name: Lemma.Energy
primitives.doc:
Felt energy: physical and emotional energy available for activity, as in
the UWES vigor items ("At my work, I feel bursting with energy", Schaufeli
et al. 2002) and the MBI exhaustion items read as depletion of the same
quantity (Maslach & Jackson 1981). Unsigned: a construct declares in its
docstring whether the construct reads high or low energy.

primitives.name: Lemma.Attention
Lemma.Identification
primitives.doc:
Identification with `target`: felt significance, involvement and
belonging (UWES dedication, Schaufeli et al. 2002; organizational
identification, Mael & Ashforth 1992; MBI cynicism read as withdrawal of
the same quantity, Maslach et al. 2001).

primitives.name: Lemma.Demand
primitives.doc:
A job demand of concrete kind `kind`: an aspect of the job requiring
sustained effort (Demerouti et al. 2001).

primitives.name: Lemma.Resource
primitives.doc:
A resource of concrete kind `kind`: an object, condition, personal
characteristic or energy valued in itself or as a means (Hobfoll 1989).

primitives.name: Lemma.Change
primitives.doc:
Signed change in a resource of kind `kind` over the construct's
horizon. Resource loss and resource gain (Hobfoll 1989) both read this
primitive, with opposite sign.

primitives.name: Lemma.Affect
primitives.doc:
Core affect located by valence and activation on the circumplex
(Russell 1980; Warr 1990).

primitives.name: Lemma.Learning
primitives.doc:
Acquisition and application of knowledge and skills (Spreitzer et al.
2005 learning; Sonnentag & Fritz 2007 mastery).

primitives.name: Lemma.Efficacy
primitives.doc:
Belief in one's capability with respect to `target` (Bandura 1977; MBI
professional efficacy, Maslach et al. 2001).

primitives.name: Lemma.Skill
primitives.doc: Perceived skill relative to the task at hand (Csikszentmihalyi 1990).

primitives.name: Lemma.Symptom
primitives.doc:
Health symptom of kind `kind` (psychosomatic complaints, depressive
symptoms, cardiovascular markers; Siegrist 1996; Hakanen et al. 2008).

primitives.name: Lemma.Performance
primitives.doc:
Work performance of kind `kind`, ideally other-reported or
administrative (Christian et al. 2011).

primitives.name: Lemma.Expectancy
primitives.doc: Generalized expectancy of `valence` outcomes (optimism, Scheier & Carver 1985).

primitives.name: Lemma.Behavior
primitives.doc: A concrete work behavior of kind `kind`.

primitives.name: Lemma.Trait
primitives.doc:
A stable personality trait of kind `kind` (Costa & McCrae 1992). A
dispositional primitive: the pilot uses traits only as moderators.

constructs.name: Lemma.Theories.Engagement.Vigor
constructs.doc:
Vigor: "high levels of energy and mental resilience while working"
(Schaufeli et al. 2002, p. 74). UWES vigor subscale. Reads high energy.

constructs.name: Lemma.Theories.Engagement.Dedication
constructs.doc:
Dedication: "a sense of significance, enthusiasm, inspiration, pride, and
challenge" in one's work (Schaufeli et al. 2002, p. 74). UWES dedication
subscale. Reads high identification with work.

constructs.name: Lemma.Theories.Engagement.Absorption
constructs.doc:
Absorption: "being fully concentrated and deeply engrossed in one's work"
(Schaufeli et al. 2002, p. 75). UWES absorption subscale.

constructs.name: Lemma.Theories.Engagement.Engagement
constructs.doc:
Work engagement: the three-factor UWES state (Schaufeli et al. 2002).
Declared with its three fields typed directly by primitives, as in the
proposal's Listing 1, so that the compiler can report which field a
competing construct shares.

constructs.name: Lemma.Theories.Engagement.TaskPerformance
constructs.doc:
In-role task performance, other-rated where possible (Christian, Garza &
Slaughter 2011).

constructs.name: Lemma.Theories.Engagement.ContextualPerformance
constructs.doc: Contextual (extra-role, citizenship) performance (Christian et al. 2011).

constructs.name: Lemma.Theories.Engagement.TurnoverIntention
constructs.doc: Intention to leave the organization (Halbesleben 2010).

constructs.name: Lemma.Theories.Burnout.Exhaustion
constructs.doc:
Emotional exhaustion: "feelings of being overextended and depleted of
one's emotional and physical resources" (Maslach et al. 2001, p. 399). MBI
exhaustion subscale. Reads low energy.

constructs.name: Lemma.Theories.Burnout.Cynicism
constructs.doc:
Cynicism (depersonalization): "a negative, callous, or excessively
detached response to various aspects of the job" (Maslach et al. 2001,
p. 399). MBI cynicism subscale. Reads withdrawal of identification with work.

constructs.name: Lemma.Theories.Burnout.ReducedEfficacy
constructs.doc:
Reduced professional efficacy: "feelings of incompetence and a lack of
achievement and productivity at work" (Maslach et al. 2001, p. 399). MBI
efficacy subscale, reversed.

constructs.name: Lemma.Theories.Burnout.Burnout
constructs.doc: Burnout as the three-dimensional MBI syndrome (Maslach & Jackson 1981).

constructs.name: Lemma.Theories.JDR.JobDemands
constructs.doc:
Job demands: "those physical, psychological, social, or organizational
aspects of the job that require sustained physical and/or psychological
(cognitive and emotional) effort" (Bakker & Demerouti 2007, p. 312).
Bundle of the demand kinds listed in Demerouti et al. 2001 (work overload,
time pressure, emotional demands, physical demands) and Bakker & Demerouti
2007 (role conflict, cognitive demands).

constructs.name: Lemma.Theories.JDR.JobResources
constructs.doc:
Job resources: "those physical, psychological, social, or organizational
aspects of the job that are functional in achieving work goals, reduce job
demands, or stimulate personal growth, learning, and development" (Bakker &
Demerouti 2007, p. 312). Bundle of autonomy, social support, performance
feedback, development opportunities and job security (Demerouti et al.
2001; Bakker & Demerouti 2007).

constructs.name: Lemma.Theories.JDR.PersonalResources
constructs.doc:
Personal resources: self-efficacy, organization-based self-esteem and
optimism (Xanthopoulou, Bakker, Demerouti & Schaufeli 2007).

constructs.name: Lemma.Theories.JDR.HealthComplaints
constructs.doc:
Psychosomatic health complaints (Hakanen, Bakker & Schaufeli 2006;
Hakanen, Schaufeli & Ahola 2008).

constructs.name: Lemma.Theories.JDR.OrganizationalCommitment
constructs.doc:
Affective organizational commitment: identification with and involvement
in the organization (Meyer & Allen 1991), as used in Hakanen et al. 2008.

constructs.name: Lemma.Theories.COR.Resources
constructs.doc:
Resources: "those objects, personal characteristics, conditions, or
energies that are valued by the individual or that serve as a means for
attainment of these objects, personal characteristics, conditions, or
energies" (Hobfoll 1989, p. 516). Bundle of concrete conditions (control,
support, security, status, advancement), energies (time, money, knowledge),
objects, and personal characteristics (self-efficacy, optimism).

constructs.name: Lemma.Theories.COR.ResourceLoss
constructs.doc:
Resource loss: actual decline in valued resources over the horizon
(Hobfoll 1989, Principle 1). Reads negative change.

constructs.name: Lemma.Theories.COR.ResourceGain
constructs.doc:
Resource gain: increase in valued resources over the horizon following
investment (Hobfoll 1989, Principle 2; Hobfoll 2001, Corollary 3). Reads
positive change.

constructs.name: Lemma.Theories.COR.Strain
constructs.doc:
Psychological strain: negative high-activation affect together with
psychosomatic symptoms (Hobfoll 1989; Hobfoll et al. 2018).

constructs.name: Lemma.Theories.ERI.Effort
Lemma.Theories.ERI.Reward
constructs.doc:
Occupational reward: money, esteem, and career opportunities including
job security (Siegrist 1996, p. 30).

constructs.name: Lemma.Theories.ERI.EffortRewardImbalance
constructs.doc:
Effort-reward imbalance: the ratio of effort to reward (Siegrist et al.
2004). Declared as the product of the two bundles; the ratio is a
measurement model over the product.

constructs.name: Lemma.Theories.ERI.Overcommitment
constructs.doc:
Overcommitment: "a set of attitudes, behaviours and emotions reflecting
excessive striving in combination with a strong desire of being approved
and esteemed", including inability to withdraw from work obligations
(Siegrist et al. 2004, p. 1486). A personal pattern, declared static.

constructs.name: Lemma.Theories.Thriving.Vitality
constructs.doc:
Vitality: "the positive feeling of having energy available" (Spreitzer
et al. 2005, p. 539; Porath et al. 2012 vitality subscale). Reads high energy.

constructs.name: Lemma.Theories.Thriving.LearningAtWork
constructs.doc:
Learning: "the sense that one is acquiring, and can apply, knowledge and
skills" (Spreitzer et al. 2005, p. 538; Porath et al. 2012 learning subscale).

constructs.name: Lemma.Theories.Thriving.Thriving
constructs.doc:
Thriving: the joint experience of vitality and learning (Spreitzer et al.
2005; Porath et al. 2012).

constructs.name: Lemma.Theories.Thriving.AgenticBehaviors
constructs.doc:
Agentic work behaviors: task focus, exploration and heedful relating
(Spreitzer et al. 2005, pp. 540-542).

constructs.name: Lemma.Theories.Thriving.UnitAgenticBehaviors
constructs.doc:
Unit-level mean of agentic work behaviors, the aggregated form through
which the pilot states Spreitzer et al.'s unit-to-individual propositions.

constructs.name: Lemma.Theories.Thriving.DecisionDiscretion
constructs.doc: Decision-making discretion in the unit (Spreitzer et al. 2005, p. 542).

constructs.name: Lemma.Theories.Thriving.InformationSharing
constructs.doc: Broad information sharing in the unit (Spreitzer et al. 2005, p. 543).

constructs.name: Lemma.Theories.Thriving.TrustClimate
constructs.doc: Climate of trust and respect in the unit (Spreitzer et al. 2005, p. 543).

constructs.name: Lemma.Theories.Recovery.Detachment
constructs.doc:
Psychological detachment from work during off-job time: mentally
disengaging from work (Sonnentag & Fritz 2007, Recovery Experience
Questionnaire). Reads low attention to work.

constructs.name: Lemma.Theories.Recovery.Relaxation
constructs.doc:
Relaxation: low activation and positive affect during off-job time
(Sonnentag & Fritz 2007).

constructs.name: Lemma.Theories.Recovery.Mastery
constructs.doc:
Mastery experiences: off-job activities that offer learning and
challenge (Sonnentag & Fritz 2007).

constructs.name: Lemma.Theories.Recovery.LeisureControl
constructs.doc:
Control during leisure time: deciding which activity to pursue and when
(Sonnentag & Fritz 2007).

constructs.name: Lemma.Theories.Recovery.WeeklyDetachment
constructs.doc:
Weekly mean of daily detachment, the form in which detachment enters
weekly propositions (Sonnentag, Binnewies & Mojza 2010 measure detachment
with a general-time-frame scale).

constructs.name: Lemma.Theories.Recovery.DailyEngagement
constructs.doc: Daily (state) work engagement (Sonnentag 2003; Bakker 2014).

constructs.name: Lemma.Theories.Flow.Flow
constructs.doc:
Flow at work: absorption, enjoyment and intrinsic motivation during a
work episode (Bakker 2008, WOLF).

constructs.name: Lemma.Theories.Flow.FlowFrequency
constructs.doc:
Weekly frequency of flow episodes (Bakker 2008 reports the WOLF over a
two-week frame; Demerouti et al. 2012 use daily measures).

constructs.name: Lemma.Theories.Flow.FlowProneness
constructs.doc:
Dispositional proneness to flow (Csikszentmihalyi 1990, autotelic
personality; Vallerand et al. 2003 use a general flow measure).

constructs.name: Lemma.Theories.Flow.ChallengeSkillBalance
constructs.doc: Perceived balance of task challenge and skill (Csikszentmihalyi 1990).

constructs.name: Lemma.Theories.Flow.Conscientiousness
constructs.doc: Conscientiousness (Costa & McCrae 1992), used as a moderator.

constructs.name: Lemma.Theories.Passion.HarmoniousPassion
constructs.doc:
Harmonious passion: autonomous internalization of work into identity
(Vallerand et al. 2003, Passion Scale, harmonious subscale).

constructs.name: Lemma.Theories.Passion.ObsessivePassion
constructs.doc:
Obsessive passion: controlled internalization of work into identity,
with felt pressure to engage (Vallerand et al. 2003, obsessive subscale).

constructs.name: Lemma.Theories.Workaholism.WorkingExcessively
constructs.doc:
Working excessively: devoting an exceptional amount of time to work
(DUWAS WE subscale). Reads working hours.

constructs.name: Lemma.Theories.Workaholism.WorkingCompulsively
constructs.doc:
Working compulsively: an inner compulsion to work (DUWAS WC subscale).
Reads controlled motivation.

constructs.name: Lemma.Theories.Workaholism.Workaholism
constructs.doc:
Workaholism: the conjunction of working excessively and compulsively
(Schaufeli, Taris & Bakker 2008).

constructs.name: Lemma.Theories.ShiromVigor.ShiromVigor
constructs.doc:
Vigor (Shirom 2003): physical strength and emotional energy. The
cognitive-liveliness facet has no primitive in the pilot vocabulary and is
omitted, which the docstring records as a fidelity limitation.

constructs.name: Lemma.Theories.ChallengeHindrance.ChallengeDemands
constructs.doc:
Challenge demands: workload, time pressure and responsibility
(Cavanaugh et al. 2000; Crawford et al. 2010).

constructs.name: Lemma.Theories.ChallengeHindrance.HindranceDemands
constructs.doc:
Hindrance demands: role conflict, role ambiguity and administrative
hassles (Cavanaugh et al. 2000; Crawford et al. 2010).

constructs.name: Lemma.Theories.Team.TeamEngagement
constructs.doc:
Team work engagement: a shared positive state of the team (Costa, Passos
& Bakker 2014), with the same three facets at the team level.

constructs.name: Lemma.Theories.Team.TeamPerformance
constructs.doc: Team task performance (Torrente et al. 2012, supervisor-rated).

constructs.name: Lemma.Generated.BakkerDemerouti2007.JobDemands
constructs.doc:
Job demands: aspects of the job requiring sustained effort; work pressure,
emotional demands, role conflict (Bakker & Demerouti 2007, p. 312).

constructs.name: Lemma.Generated.BakkerDemerouti2007.JobResources
constructs.doc:
Job resources: autonomy, social support, performance feedback, development
opportunities (Bakker & Demerouti 2007, p. 312).

constructs.name: Lemma.Generated.Hobfoll1989.Resources
constructs.doc: Resources: objects, conditions, personal characteristics, energies (Hobfoll 1989, p. 516).

constructs.name: Lemma.Generated.Hobfoll1989.NetLoss
constructs.doc: Net resource loss over the horizon (Hobfoll 1989, p. 516).

constructs.name: Lemma.Generated.Hobfoll1989.StressReaction
constructs.doc: Psychological stress reaction (Hobfoll 1989, p. 516).

constructs.name: Lemma.Generated.MaslachJackson1981.EmotionalExhaustion
constructs.doc: Emotional exhaustion (Maslach & Jackson 1981, p. 99).

constructs.name: Lemma.Generated.MaslachJackson1981.Depersonalization
constructs.doc: Depersonalization: an impersonal response toward recipients (Maslach & Jackson 1981, p. 99).

constructs.name: Lemma.Generated.MaslachJackson1981.ReducedAccomplishment
constructs.doc: Reduced personal accomplishment (Maslach & Jackson 1981, p. 99).

constructs.name: Lemma.Generated.Schaufeli2002.Vigor
constructs.doc: Vigor: energy and mental resilience while working (Schaufeli et al. 2002, p. 74).

constructs.name: Lemma.Generated.Schaufeli2002.Dedication
constructs.doc: Dedication: significance, enthusiasm, inspiration, pride, challenge (Schaufeli et al. 2002, p. 74).

constructs.name: Lemma.Generated.Schaufeli2002.Absorption
constructs.doc: Absorption: full concentration and engrossment in work (Schaufeli et al. 2002, p. 75).

constructs.name: Lemma.Generated.Schaufeli2002.WorkEngagement
constructs.doc: Work engagement as the three correlated factors (Schaufeli et al. 2002).

constructs.name: Lemma.Generated.Siegrist1996.Effort
constructs.doc: Extrinsic effort: time pressure, interruptions, responsibility, overload (Siegrist 1996, p. 30).

constructs.name: Lemma.Generated.Siegrist1996.Reward
constructs.doc: Reward: money, esteem, status control (Siegrist 1996, p. 30).

constructs.name: Lemma.Generated.Siegrist1996.Imbalance
constructs.doc: Effort-reward imbalance (Siegrist 1996).

constructs.name: Lemma.Generated.Siegrist1996.Overcommitment
constructs.doc: Overcommitment: excessive striving and inability to withdraw (Siegrist 1996, p. 31).

constructs.name: Lemma.Generated.Siegrist1996.CardiovascularStrain
constructs.doc: Cardiovascular strain: negative affect and cardiovascular symptoms (Siegrist 1996).

constructs.name: Lemma.Generated.Spreitzer2005.Vitality
constructs.doc: Vitality: the positive feeling of having energy available (Spreitzer et al. 2005, p. 539).

constructs.name: Lemma.Generated.Spreitzer2005.Learning
constructs.doc: Learning: acquiring and applying knowledge and skills (Spreitzer et al. 2005, p. 538).

constructs.name: Lemma.Generated.Spreitzer2005.Thriving
constructs.doc: Thriving: vitality and learning jointly (Spreitzer et al. 2005, p. 538).

propositions.name: Lemma.Theories.Engagement.engagement_task_performance
propositions.doc:
Engagement predicts task performance (Christian et al. 2011,
meta-analysis, ρ = .43 with task performance).
propositions.citation: Christian, Garza & Slaughter 2011, Personnel Psychology 64, 89-136

propositions.name: Lemma.Theories.Engagement.engagement_contextual_performance
propositions.doc:
Engagement predicts contextual performance (Christian et al. 2011,
ρ = .34 with contextual performance).
propositions.citation: Christian, Garza & Slaughter 2011, Personnel Psychology 64, 89-136

propositions.name: Lemma.Theories.Engagement.engagement_turnover
propositions.doc:
Engagement is negatively related to turnover intention (Halbesleben 2010,
meta-analysis of the JD-R engagement literature).
propositions.citation: Halbesleben 2010, in Bakker & Leiter (eds.) Work Engagement, 102-117

propositions.name: Lemma.Theories.Burnout.exhaustion_cynicism
propositions.doc:
Exhaustion leads to cynicism over time: the sequential model (Leiter &
Maslach 1988; Maslach et al. 2001, p. 403; Taris, Le Blanc, Schaufeli &
Schreurs 2005, longitudinal).
propositions.citation: Leiter & Maslach 1988, J. Organ. Behav. 9, 297-308; Taris et al. 2005, Work & Stress 19, 238-255

propositions.name: Lemma.Theories.Burnout.cynicism_reduced_efficacy
propositions.doc:
Cynicism leads to reduced efficacy: the third step of the sequential
model (Leiter & Maslach 1988).
propositions.citation: Leiter & Maslach 1988, J. Organ. Behav. 9, 297-308

propositions.name: Lemma.Theories.Burnout.burnout_task_performance
propositions.doc:
Burnout is negatively related to in-role performance (Taris 2006,
meta-analysis; Swider & Zimmerman 2010, meta-analysis).
propositions.citation: Taris 2006, Work & Stress 20, 316-334; Swider & Zimmerman 2010, J. Vocat. Behav. 76, 487-506

propositions.name: Lemma.Theories.Burnout.exhaustion_task_performance
propositions.doc: Exhaustion is negatively related to in-role performance (Taris 2006).
propositions.citation: Taris 2006, Work & Stress 20, 316-334

propositions.name: Lemma.Theories.Burnout.burnout_turnover
propositions.doc:
Burnout predicts turnover intention (Swider & Zimmerman 2010; Lee &
Ashforth 1996).
propositions.citation: Swider & Zimmerman 2010, J. Vocat. Behav. 76, 487-506

propositions.name: Lemma.Theories.JDR.demands_exhaustion
propositions.doc:
Job demands predict exhaustion (Demerouti et al. 2001; Alarcon 2011,
meta-analysis; Lesener, Gusy & Wolter 2019, meta-analysis of longitudinal
studies).
propositions.citation: Alarcon 2011, J. Vocat. Behav. 79, 549-562; Lesener, Gusy & Wolter 2019, Work & Stress 33, 76-103

propositions.name: Lemma.Theories.JDR.demands_exhaustion_buffered
propositions.doc:
Job demands predict exhaustion less strongly when job resources are high:
the buffer hypothesis (Bakker, Demerouti & Euwema 2005; Bakker & Demerouti
2007, p. 314).
propositions.citation: Bakker, Demerouti & Euwema 2005, J. Occup. Health Psychol. 10, 170-180

propositions.name: Lemma.Theories.JDR.exhaustion_health
propositions.doc:
Exhaustion predicts health complaints (Hakanen, Schaufeli & Ahola 2008,
three-year cross-lagged study; health-impairment process).
propositions.citation: Hakanen, Schaufeli & Ahola 2008, Work & Stress 22, 224-241

propositions.name: Lemma.Theories.JDR.resources_engagement
propositions.doc:
Job resources predict engagement (Schaufeli & Bakker 2004; Christian et
al. 2011; Halbesleben 2010, meta-analyses).
propositions.citation: Halbesleben 2010; Christian, Garza & Slaughter 2011, Personnel Psychology 64, 89-136

propositions.name: Lemma.Theories.JDR.resources_engagement_boosted
propositions.doc:
Job resources predict engagement more strongly when job demands are high:
the boost hypothesis (Bakker, Hakanen, Demerouti & Xanthopoulou 2007).
propositions.citation: Bakker, Hakanen, Demerouti & Xanthopoulou 2007, J. Educ. Psychol. 99, 274-284

propositions.name: Lemma.Theories.JDR.resources_exhaustion
propositions.doc:
Lack of job resources predicts exhaustion: resources are negatively
related to burnout (Schaufeli & Bakker 2004; Lee & Ashforth 1996,
meta-analysis; Alarcon 2011).
propositions.citation: Lee & Ashforth 1996, J. Appl. Psychol. 81, 123-133; Alarcon 2011, J. Vocat. Behav. 79, 549-562

propositions.name: Lemma.Theories.JDR.demands_engagement
propositions.doc:
Job demands are unrelated to engagement in the dual-process model:
"engagement is exclusively predicted by available job resources" (Schaufeli
& Bakker 2004, abstract; four-sample structural model).
propositions.citation: Schaufeli & Bakker 2004, J. Organ. Behav. 25, 293-315

propositions.name: Lemma.Theories.JDR.personal_resources_engagement
propositions.doc:
Personal resources predict engagement (Xanthopoulou et al. 2007;
Xanthopoulou, Bakker, Demerouti & Schaufeli 2009, two-wave study).
propositions.citation: Xanthopoulou, Bakker, Demerouti & Schaufeli 2009, J. Vocat. Behav. 74, 235-244

propositions.name: Lemma.Theories.JDR.engagement_resources
propositions.doc:
Engagement predicts job resources over time: the gain cycle (Xanthopoulou
et al. 2009; Hakanen, Perhoniemi & Toppinen-Tanner 2008).
propositions.citation: Xanthopoulou et al. 2009, J. Vocat. Behav. 74, 235-244; Hakanen, Perhoniemi & Toppinen-Tanner 2008, J. Vocat. Behav. 73, 78-91

propositions.name: Lemma.Theories.JDR.engagement_commitment
propositions.doc:
Engagement predicts organizational commitment (Hakanen, Schaufeli & Ahola
2008, three-year cross-lagged study).
propositions.citation: Hakanen, Schaufeli & Ahola 2008, Work & Stress 22, 224-241

propositions.name: Lemma.Theories.JDR.demands_task_performance
propositions.doc:
Job demands are negatively related to in-role performance through
exhaustion (Bakker, Demerouti & Verbeke 2004).
propositions.citation: Bakker, Demerouti & Verbeke 2004, Hum. Resour. Manage. 43, 83-104

propositions.name: Lemma.Theories.COR.loss_strain
propositions.doc:
Resource loss produces strain (Hobfoll 1989, Principle 1; Hobfoll 2001;
Hobfoll et al. 2018 review the longitudinal evidence).
propositions.citation: Hobfoll 1989, Am. Psychol. 44, 513-524; Hobfoll et al. 2018, Annu. Rev. Organ. Psychol. Organ. Behav. 5, 103-128

propositions.name: Lemma.Theories.COR.gain_strain
propositions.doc:
Resource gain reduces strain, with a smaller effect than loss (Hobfoll
2001, primacy of loss).
propositions.citation: Hobfoll 2001, Appl. Psychol. 50, 337-421

propositions.name: Lemma.Theories.COR.resources_strain
propositions.doc:
Those with greater resources are less vulnerable to strain (Hobfoll
1989; Halbesleben 2006, meta-analysis of social support and burnout).
propositions.citation: Hobfoll 1989, Am. Psychol. 44, 513-524; Halbesleben 2006, J. Appl. Psychol. 91, 1134-1145

propositions.name: Lemma.Theories.COR.loss_exhaustion
propositions.doc:
Resource loss produces emotional exhaustion: COR applied to burnout
(Hobfoll & Freedy 1993; Lee & Ashforth 1996, meta-analysis).
propositions.citation: Hobfoll & Freedy 1993, in Schaufeli, Maslach & Marek (eds.) Professional Burnout; Lee & Ashforth 1996, J. Appl. Psychol. 81, 123-133

propositions.name: Lemma.Theories.COR.demands_loss
propositions.doc:
Job demands deplete resources (Hobfoll & Freedy 1993; Hobfoll et al.
2018, p. 108: demands lead to resource loss).
propositions.citation: Hobfoll & Freedy 1993; Hobfoll et al. 2018, Annu. Rev. Organ. Psychol. Organ. Behav. 5, 103-128

propositions.name: Lemma.Theories.COR.strain_loss
propositions.doc:
Strain produces further resource loss: the loss spiral (Hobfoll 2001,
Corollary 2; Demerouti, Bakker & Bulters 2004, three-wave study).
propositions.citation: Hobfoll 2001, Appl. Psychol. 50, 337-421; Demerouti, Bakker & Bulters 2004, J. Vocat. Behav. 64, 131-149

propositions.name: Lemma.Theories.COR.resources_gain
propositions.doc:
Those with resources are better positioned to gain: the gain spiral
(Hobfoll 2001, Corollary 3).
propositions.citation: Hobfoll 2001, Appl. Psychol. 50, 337-421

propositions.name: Lemma.Theories.COR.gain_engagement
propositions.doc:
Resource gain produces engagement: engagement is a resource-gain process
(Hobfoll et al. 2018; Xanthopoulou et al. 2009).
propositions.citation: Hobfoll et al. 2018, Annu. Rev. Organ. Psychol. Organ. Behav. 5, 103-128; Xanthopoulou et al. 2009, J. Vocat. Behav. 74, 235-244

propositions.name: Lemma.Theories.ERI.imbalance_strain
propositions.citation: Siegrist 1996, J. Occup. Health Psychol. 1, 27-41; Dragano et al. 2017, Epidemiology 28, 619-626

propositions.name: Lemma.Theories.ERI.overcommitment_strain
propositions.doc:
Overcommitment predicts strain on its own (Siegrist 1996; van Vegchel et
al. 2005). Declared static so that the consequent is routed through the
chronic-strain temporal rule below.
propositions.citation: van Vegchel, de Jonge, Bosma & Schaufeli 2005, Soc. Sci. Med. 60, 1117-1131

propositions.name: Lemma.Theories.ERI.imbalance_strain_overcommitted
propositions.doc:
Overcommitment amplifies the effect of imbalance on strain: the
interaction hypothesis (Siegrist 1996; Siegrist et al. 2004). Evidence is
mixed (van Vegchel et al. 2005).
propositions.citation: Siegrist et al. 2004, Soc. Sci. Med. 58, 1483-1499; van Vegchel et al. 2005

propositions.name: Lemma.Theories.ERI.reward_strain
propositions.doc:
Low reward predicts strain (Siegrist 1996; van Vegchel et al. 2005
report reward main effects).
propositions.citation: van Vegchel et al. 2005, Soc. Sci. Med. 60, 1117-1131

propositions.name: Lemma.Theories.ERI.effort_strain
propositions.doc:
High effort predicts strain (van Vegchel et al. 2005 report effort main
effects).
propositions.citation: van Vegchel et al. 2005, Soc. Sci. Med. 60, 1117-1131

propositions.name: Lemma.Theories.ERI.imbalance_exhaustion
propositions.doc:
Effort-reward imbalance predicts emotional exhaustion (Bakker, Killmer,
Siegrist & Schaufeli 2000, nurses).
propositions.citation: Bakker, Killmer, Siegrist & Schaufeli 2000, J. Adv. Nurs. 31, 884-891

propositions.name: Lemma.Theories.Thriving.discretion_agentic
propositions.doc:
Decision-making discretion enables agentic behaviors (Spreitzer et al.
2005, Proposition 4). Stated at the unit level over the aggregated
behaviors.
propositions.citation: Spreitzer et al. 2005, Organ. Sci. 16, 537-549, Proposition 4

propositions.name: Lemma.Theories.Thriving.information_agentic
propositions.doc:
Broad information sharing enables agentic behaviors (Spreitzer et al.
2005, Proposition 5).
propositions.citation: Spreitzer et al. 2005, Organ. Sci. 16, 537-549, Proposition 5

propositions.name: Lemma.Theories.Thriving.trust_agentic
propositions.doc:
A climate of trust and respect enables agentic behaviors (Spreitzer et
al. 2005, Proposition 6).
propositions.citation: Spreitzer et al. 2005, Organ. Sci. 16, 537-549, Proposition 6

propositions.name: Lemma.Theories.Thriving.agentic_thriving
propositions.doc:
Agentic behaviors produce thriving (Spreitzer et al. 2005, Propositions
1-3; Niessen, Sonnentag & Sach 2012, diary study of task focus and
exploration).
propositions.citation: Spreitzer et al. 2005; Niessen, Sonnentag & Sach 2012, J. Organ. Behav. 33, 468-487

propositions.name: Lemma.Theories.Thriving.thriving_task_performance
propositions.doc:
Thriving is positively related to job performance (Porath et al. 2012,
supervisor ratings; Kleine, Rudolph & Zacher 2019, meta-analysis).
propositions.citation: Porath, Spreitzer, Gibson & Garnett 2012, J. Organ. Behav. 33, 250-275; Kleine, Rudolph & Zacher 2019, J. Organ. Behav. 40, 973-999

propositions.name: Lemma.Theories.Thriving.thriving_health
propositions.doc:
Thriving is negatively related to health complaints (Spreitzer et al.
2005, Proposition 8; Porath et al. 2012; Kleine et al. 2019).
propositions.citation: Kleine, Rudolph & Zacher 2019, J. Organ. Behav. 40, 973-999

propositions.name: Lemma.Theories.Thriving.thriving_burnout
propositions.doc:
Thriving is negatively related to burnout (Porath et al. 2012; Kleine et
al. 2019).
propositions.citation: Porath et al. 2012, J. Organ. Behav. 33, 250-275; Kleine, Rudolph & Zacher 2019

propositions.name: Lemma.Theories.Recovery.detachment_exhaustion
propositions.citation: Sonnentag, Binnewies & Mojza 2010, J. Appl. Psychol. 95, 965-976

propositions.name: Lemma.Theories.Recovery.detachment_daily_engagement
propositions.doc:
Evening detachment predicts next-day engagement (Sonnentag, Mojza,
Binnewies & Scholl 2008, diary study).
propositions.citation: Sonnentag, Mojza, Binnewies & Scholl 2008, Work & Stress 22, 257-276

propositions.name: Lemma.Theories.Recovery.demands_engagement_detachment
propositions.doc:
Job demands are negatively related to engagement, and detachment buffers
the relation (Sonnentag, Binnewies & Mojza 2010, one-year study). Stated
with the moderator, so the compiler records a conditional disagreement,
not a contradiction, with JD-R's null main effect.
propositions.citation: Sonnentag, Binnewies & Mojza 2010, J. Appl. Psychol. 95, 965-976

propositions.name: Lemma.Theories.Recovery.demands_health_detachment
propositions.doc:
Job demands predict psychosomatic complaints, and detachment buffers the
relation (Sonnentag, Binnewies & Mojza 2010).
propositions.citation: Sonnentag, Binnewies & Mojza 2010, J. Appl. Psychol. 95, 965-976

propositions.name: Lemma.Theories.Recovery.relaxation_daily_engagement
propositions.doc:
Relaxation during off-job time predicts next-morning vigor through
feeling recovered (Sonnentag, Binnewies & Mojza 2008; Binnewies, Sonnentag
& Mojza 2009). Stated over daily engagement.
propositions.citation: Sonnentag, Binnewies & Mojza 2008, J. Appl. Psychol. 93, 674-684

propositions.name: Lemma.Theories.Flow.balance_flow
propositions.doc:
Challenge-skill balance produces flow (Csikszentmihalyi 1990;
Csikszentmihalyi & LeFevre 1989, experience sampling).
propositions.citation: Csikszentmihalyi & LeFevre 1989, J. Pers. Soc. Psychol. 56, 815-822

propositions.name: Lemma.Theories.Flow.resources_flow
propositions.doc:
Job resources predict flow (Bakker 2005, music teachers; Bakker 2008,
Study 2). Stated weekly and routed through `flowWeekly`.
propositions.citation: Bakker 2005, J. Vocat. Behav. 66, 26-44; Bakker 2008, J. Vocat. Behav. 72, 400-414

propositions.name: Lemma.Theories.Flow.flow_task_performance_conscientious
propositions.doc:
Flow predicts in-role performance for conscientious employees
(Demerouti 2006).
propositions.citation: Demerouti 2006, J. Occup. Health Psychol. 11, 266-280

propositions.name: Lemma.Theories.Flow.flow_vigor_detached
propositions.doc:
Flow at work predicts energy after work when employees detach in the
evening (Demerouti, Bakker, Sonnentag & Fullagar 2012, diary study).
propositions.citation: Demerouti, Bakker, Sonnentag & Fullagar 2012, J. Organ. Behav. 33, 276-295

propositions.name: Lemma.Theories.Passion.obsessive_exhaustion
propositions.doc:
Obsessive passion predicts emotional exhaustion over six months
(Vallerand et al. 2010, Study 2, nurses). The static antecedent enters the
weekly proposition by the static-embedding rule.
propositions.citation: Vallerand, Paquet, Philippe & Charest 2010, J. Pers. 78, 289-312

propositions.name: Lemma.Theories.Passion.harmonious_exhaustion
propositions.doc:
Harmonious passion is negatively related to emotional exhaustion
(Vallerand et al. 2010, Studies 1 and 2).
propositions.citation: Vallerand, Paquet, Philippe & Charest 2010, J. Pers. 78, 289-312

propositions.name: Lemma.Theories.Passion.harmonious_flow
propositions.doc:
Harmonious passion is positively related to flow (Vallerand et al.
2003, Study 1). Stated at the static horizon over flow proneness.
propositions.citation: Vallerand et al. 2003, J. Pers. Soc. Psychol. 85, 756-767

propositions.name: Lemma.Theories.Passion.obsessive_flow
propositions.doc: Obsessive passion is unrelated to flow (Vallerand et al. 2003, Study 1).
propositions.citation: Vallerand et al. 2003, J. Pers. Soc. Psychol. 85, 756-767

propositions.name: Lemma.Theories.Passion.harmonious_engagement
propositions.doc:
Harmonious passion is positively related to vigor and dedication
(Vallerand et al. 2010 report positive relations with work satisfaction;
Forest, Mageau, Sarrazin & Morin 2011 report relations with vitality).
Stated over engagement.
propositions.citation: Forest, Mageau, Sarrazin & Morin 2011, Can. J. Adm. Sci. 28, 27-40

propositions.name: Lemma.Theories.Workaholism.workaholism_exhaustion
propositions.doc:
Workaholism is positively related to exhaustion (Schaufeli, Taris & van
Rhenen 2008; Clark, Michel, Zhdanova, Pui & Baltes 2016, meta-analysis).
propositions.citation: Clark, Michel, Zhdanova, Pui & Baltes 2016, J. Manage. 42, 1836-1873

propositions.name: Lemma.Theories.Workaholism.excessive_engagement
propositions.doc:
Working excessively is positively related to engagement, working
compulsively is not (Schaufeli, Taris & van Rhenen 2008). Stated for the
excessive component.
propositions.citation: Schaufeli, Taris & van Rhenen 2008, Appl. Psychol. 57, 173-203

propositions.name: Lemma.Theories.Workaholism.compulsive_engagement
propositions.doc:
Working compulsively is unrelated to engagement (Schaufeli, Taris & van
Rhenen 2008).
propositions.citation: Schaufeli, Taris & van Rhenen 2008, Appl. Psychol. 57, 173-203

propositions.name: Lemma.Theories.Workaholism.workaholism_health
propositions.doc:
Workaholism is positively related to health complaints (Clark et al.
2016).
propositions.citation: Clark, Michel, Zhdanova, Pui & Baltes 2016, J. Manage. 42, 1836-1873

propositions.name: Lemma.Theories.ShiromVigor.vigor_health
propositions.doc:
Vigor predicts better self-rated health (Shirom 2011; Shirom, Toker,
Berliner, Shapira & Melamed 2008, longitudinal).
propositions.citation: Shirom, Toker, Berliner, Shapira & Melamed 2008, J. Occup. Health Psychol. 13, 319-333

propositions.name: Lemma.Theories.ShiromVigor.vigor_task_performance
propositions.doc:
Vigor predicts job performance (Shirom 2011 review; Carmeli, Ben-Hador,
Waldman & Rupp 2009).
propositions.citation: Carmeli, Ben-Hador, Waldman & Rupp 2009, J. Appl. Psychol. 94, 1553-1561

propositions.name: Lemma.Theories.ChallengeHindrance.challenge_engagement
propositions.doc:
Challenge demands are positively related to engagement (Crawford, LePine
& Rich 2010, meta-analysis, ρ = .21).
propositions.citation: Crawford, LePine & Rich 2010, J. Appl. Psychol. 95, 834-848

propositions.name: Lemma.Theories.ChallengeHindrance.hindrance_engagement
propositions.doc:
Hindrance demands are negatively related to engagement (Crawford et al.
2010, ρ = -.19).
propositions.citation: Crawford, LePine & Rich 2010, J. Appl. Psychol. 95, 834-848

propositions.name: Lemma.Theories.ChallengeHindrance.challenge_exhaustion
propositions.doc:
Challenge demands are positively related to burnout (Crawford et al.
2010). Stated over exhaustion.
propositions.citation: Crawford, LePine & Rich 2010, J. Appl. Psychol. 95, 834-848

propositions.name: Lemma.Theories.ChallengeHindrance.hindrance_exhaustion
propositions.doc:
Hindrance demands are positively related to burnout (Crawford et al.
2010). Stated over exhaustion.
propositions.citation: Crawford, LePine & Rich 2010, J. Appl. Psychol. 95, 834-848

propositions.name: Lemma.Theories.ChallengeHindrance.challenge_task_performance
propositions.doc:
Challenge stressors are positively related to performance (LePine,
Podsakoff & LePine 2005, meta-analysis).
propositions.citation: LePine, Podsakoff & LePine 2005, Acad. Manage. J. 48, 764-775

propositions.name: Lemma.Theories.ChallengeHindrance.hindrance_task_performance
propositions.doc:
Hindrance stressors are negatively related to performance (LePine et al.
2005).
propositions.citation: LePine, Podsakoff & LePine 2005, Acad. Manage. J. 48, 764-775

propositions.name: Lemma.Theories.BurnoutProcess.exhaustion_cynicism
propositions.doc:
Exhaustion leads to cynicism (Leiter 1993 retains this step of the
sequential model).
propositions.citation: Leiter 1993, in Schaufeli, Maslach & Marek (eds.) Professional Burnout, 237-250

propositions.name: Lemma.Theories.BurnoutProcess.cynicism_reduced_efficacy
propositions.doc:
Reduced efficacy develops in parallel with, not as a consequence of,
cynicism (Leiter 1993).
propositions.citation: Leiter 1993, in Schaufeli, Maslach & Marek (eds.) Professional Burnout, 237-250

propositions.name: Lemma.Theories.BurnoutProcess.resources_reduced_efficacy
propositions.doc:
Lack of job resources predicts reduced efficacy directly (Leiter 1993;
Maslach et al. 2001, p. 403).
propositions.citation: Leiter 1993, in Schaufeli, Maslach & Marek (eds.) Professional Burnout, 237-250

propositions.name: Lemma.Theories.BurnoutProcess.demands_exhaustion
propositions.doc:
Job demands predict exhaustion (Leiter 1993 locates the origin of
exhaustion in demands).
propositions.citation: Leiter 1993, in Schaufeli, Maslach & Marek (eds.) Professional Burnout, 237-250

propositions.name: Lemma.Theories.Activation.demands_task_performance
propositions.doc:
Job demands relate to in-role performance in an inverted-U shape
(Janssen 2001, Hypothesis 1; Gardner 1986).
propositions.citation: Janssen 2001, Acad. Manage. J. 44, 1039-1050; Gardner 1986, Acad. Manage. Rev. 11, 411-418

propositions.name: Lemma.Theories.Team.team_engagement_performance
propositions.doc: Team engagement predicts team performance (Torrente et al. 2012).
propositions.citation: Torrente, Salanova, Llorens & Schaufeli 2012, Psicothema 24, 106-112

propositions.name: Lemma.Theories.Team.engagement_team_performance
propositions.doc:
Team-level engagement relates to individual engagement through
crossover (Bakker, van Emmerik & Euwema 2006). Stated at the team level
over the aggregate, routed through `engagementTeam`.
propositions.citation: Bakker, van Emmerik & Euwema 2006, Work Occup. 33, 464-489

propositions.name: Lemma.Generated.BakkerDemerouti2007.demands_exhaustion
propositions.doc: Job demands predict exhaustion (Bakker & Demerouti 2007, p. 313, health impairment process).
propositions.citation: Bakker & Demerouti 2007, J. Manag. Psychol. 22, 309-328

propositions.name: Lemma.Generated.BakkerDemerouti2007.resources_engagement
propositions.doc: Job resources predict engagement (Bakker & Demerouti 2007, p. 313, motivational process).
propositions.citation: Bakker & Demerouti 2007, J. Manag. Psychol. 22, 309-328

propositions.name: Lemma.Generated.BakkerDemerouti2007.demands_exhaustion_buffered
propositions.doc: Job resources buffer the effect of demands on exhaustion (Bakker & Demerouti 2007, p. 314).
propositions.citation: Bakker & Demerouti 2007, J. Manag. Psychol. 22, 309-328

propositions.name: Lemma.Generated.BakkerDemerouti2007.resources_engagement_boosted
propositions.doc: Resources matter most for engagement when demands are high (Bakker & Demerouti 2007, p. 315).
propositions.citation: Bakker & Demerouti 2007, J. Manag. Psychol. 22, 309-328

propositions.name: Lemma.Generated.BakkerDemerouti2007.engagement_performance
propositions.doc: Engagement predicts in-role performance (Bakker & Demerouti 2007, p. 316).
propositions.citation: Bakker & Demerouti 2007, J. Manag. Psychol. 22, 309-328

propositions.name: Lemma.Generated.Hobfoll1989.loss_stress
propositions.doc: Resource loss produces stress (Hobfoll 1989, p. 516).
propositions.citation: Hobfoll 1989, Am. Psychol. 44, 513-524

propositions.name: Lemma.Generated.Hobfoll1989.resources_stress
propositions.doc: Those with more resources are less vulnerable to stress (Hobfoll 1989, p. 517).
propositions.citation: Hobfoll 1989, Am. Psychol. 44, 513-524

propositions.name: Lemma.Generated.Hobfoll1989.stress_loss
propositions.doc: Stress begets further loss: the loss spiral (Hobfoll 1989, p. 519).
propositions.citation: Hobfoll 1989, Am. Psychol. 44, 513-524

propositions.name: Lemma.Generated.MaslachJackson1981.exhaustion_turnover
propositions.doc: Burnout relates to intention to leave (Maslach & Jackson 1981, p. 108).
propositions.citation: Maslach & Jackson 1981, J. Occup. Behav. 2, 99-113

propositions.name: Lemma.Generated.Schaufeli2002.engagement_exhaustion
propositions.doc: Engagement is negatively related to exhaustion (Schaufeli et al. 2002, two-factor model).
propositions.citation: Schaufeli et al. 2002, J. Happiness Stud. 3, 71-92

propositions.name: Lemma.Generated.Siegrist1996.imbalance_strain
propositions.doc: Imbalance raises strain and cardiovascular risk (Siegrist 1996, prospective cohorts).
propositions.citation: Siegrist 1996, J. Occup. Health Psychol. 1, 27-41

propositions.name: Lemma.Generated.Siegrist1996.overcommitment_strain
propositions.doc: Overcommitment independently raises strain (Siegrist 1996).
propositions.citation: Siegrist 1996, J. Occup. Health Psychol. 1, 27-41

propositions.name: Lemma.Generated.Siegrist1996.imbalance_strain_overcommitted
propositions.doc: Overcommitment amplifies the imbalance effect (Siegrist 1996).
propositions.citation: Siegrist 1996, J. Occup. Health Psychol. 1, 27-41

propositions.name: Lemma.Generated.Spreitzer2005.agentic_thriving
propositions.doc: Agentic work behaviors promote thriving (Spreitzer et al. 2005, P1-P3).
propositions.citation: Spreitzer et al. 2005, Organ. Sci. 16, 537-549, P1-P3

propositions.name: Lemma.Generated.Spreitzer2005.discretion_agentic
propositions.doc: Decision-making discretion promotes agentic behaviors (Spreitzer et al. 2005, P4).
propositions.citation: Spreitzer et al. 2005, Organ. Sci. 16, 537-549, P4

propositions.name: Lemma.Generated.Spreitzer2005.thriving_health
propositions.doc: Thriving promotes health (Spreitzer et al. 2005, P8).
propositions.citation: Spreitzer et al. 2005, Organ. Sci. 16, 537-549, P8

aggregations.name: Lemma.Theories.Thriving.agenticUnitMean
aggregations.citation: Chan 1998, J. Appl. Psychol. 83, 234-246; Spreitzer et al. 2005

aggregations.name: Lemma.Theories.Team.engagementTeam
aggregations.citation: Costa, Passos & Bakker 2014, Eur. J. Work Organ. Psychol. 23, 414-429

temporals.citation: Sonnentag, Binnewies & Mojza 2010, J. Appl. Psychol. 95, 965-976

temporals.citation: Csikszentmihalyi 1990, Flow: The Psychology of Optimal Experience
